Okay so this is my current job, Mojave Valley School District, I teach at Harmon Ridge Middle School in Las Vegas, on the east side. I've been there since I came to the US, so I came over in July 2017 on a J-1, it was a teacher exchange program through this sponsor called Bridgeway Cultural Exchange, and my first day with kids was August 2017. They put me in seventh grade science that first year, five sections, and honestly I think I had like 34, 35 kids in some of those rooms. It was a lot. Coming from Cebu I thought I was ready for big classes and I was, but the behavior stuff was really different, and the paperwork, oh my gosh, the paperwork.

Anyway. I teach seventh and eighth grade science now, mostly eighth. Physical science and earth science mostly, some life science units in seventh. We follow the Nevada science standards which are basically NGSS, so everything is phenomena and three-dimensional learning and all of that, which I actually love.

The visa part matters so I'll just say it. The J-1 only goes three years for teachers, and then the district sponsored my H-1B in 2020. I got picked in the lottery that spring, it started in October 2020, they've been really good about it, HR walked me through everything and they paid the lawyer. There was also a whole waiver thing for the J-1 home residency rule, that took forever, I'm not going to get into it. I'm still on the H-1B now through the district. So if I leave I need the new company to do a transfer, that's just the reality.

Okay so the bigger stuff. I became science department lead at Harmon Ridge in 2021, the fall of 2021. That means I run the department meetings, there's me and six other science teachers, so seven of us. I do the pacing calendar, I order all the lab supplies, so I manage the science budget, it's around $9,000 a year which sounds like a lot until you price out a class set of anything. I mentor the new teachers, I think I've mentored four first-year teachers so far, maybe five if you count the long-term sub who stayed. And I sit on the school leadership team with the principal and the other department leads.

I also wrote assessments for the district. In 2022 they had a small team writing the common end-of-unit assessments for eighth grade science, and I was one of the item writers, I wrote around 60 items I think, multiple choice and some of the constructed response ones with rubrics, and then we did the item review where you look at how kids actually answered and fix the bad ones. That was honestly one of my favorite things I've done, figuring out why a question was confusing kids. Like the question is testing reading, not science, that kind of thing.

The other huge thing in this job was the Canvas unit library during remote teaching in 2020 but I'm going to tell that one separately because it's its own whole story. And the robotics club too, separate.

What else. I've done a lot of PD for other teachers, mostly about Canvas and blended learning, again I'll put that with the unit library story.

Oh, the break. I had my son in February 2023, so I was out on maternity leave from February to the end of July, about five months, a little more with the summer. The district held my spot and a long-term sub covered my classes, and she followed my unit plans which was great, the kids didn't really lose anything. I came back in August 2023 for the new school year. I'm saying it because there's a gap on paper and people ask.

My evaluations have always been the top rating, highly effective, every year since I think 2019. And I got the school's Teacher of the Year in 2022, which is voted by the staff, so that was nice.

Honestly the reason I'm thinking about leaving is not the kids. I love the kids. It's that the part of the job I'm best at, and the part I get excited about, is designing the units and the assessments and teaching the teachers. That's what I do on Sundays for fun basically. And the pay is capped, I'm at about $68,000 now with my master's credits, and I'm not going to go into administration to make more, I really don't want to be a principal.
